arms.label: Ember
evidence: The Pi 5, Active Cooler, connector inventory, power budget, and assumed display/NVMe/fan are specified carefully, but the actual display and storage hardware remain unmeasured surrogates.
Repository facts, verified hardware facts, design assumptions, unknowns, and provisional dimensions are explicitly separated.
The filtered front intake, upper and lower branches, NVMe wash, rear exhaust, recirculation gasket, clearance requirement, and fault cases form a complete airflow account.
The Active Cooler retains its dedicated native header while the exhaust fan has independent fused power, PWM, tach monitoring, and failure-response testing.
The orientation comparison, direct native-port access, plug envelopes, cable turns, strain rails, P-clamps, and touch-remapping checks address both cable and interface motion.
Captive service panels, a slide-out electronics carrier, removable filter, replaceable adapters, and retention of the installed Active Cooler preserve fragile assemblies during maintenance.

Five keys match one documented controller profile and validation covers mouse and 4/5/8-button modes, but repeated musical workflow and control ergonomics are less developed than the engineering details.
The design openly reports the failed clone, identifies every major assumption, rejects enclosure-level interpretation of fan ratings, and states what remains unproven.
The validation plan covers fit, thermal soak, dirty-filter and failed-fan cases, acoustics, airflow smoke tests, controls, power, RF, cable loads, tipping, and safety.
Dimensions, component stack, connector placement, airflow split, materials, and service strategy consistently support the selected wedge-console concept.
arms.most_consequential_strength: A highly integrated thermal, connector, and service design with unusually explicit validation requirements.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The exact display, NVMe assembly, SSD, and controller remain assumptions, while musician-facing repeated-use behavior receives comparatively limited development.

arms.label: Harbor
evidence: Native Pi hardware and cooling details are faithful and the RC070N explains the reported USB-C ambiguity, but that display identification is still only a packaging assumption.
Verified repository facts, reasonable inference, explicit assumptions, and unknown hardware are cleanly distinguished and tied to a pinned revision.
The filtered intake, quantified 70/30 split, upper display/CPU path, lower NVMe path, sealed rear exhaust, bypass control, and component-specific thermal treatments are comprehensive.
The Active Cooler remains independently controlled while the rear fan has its own PWM/tach board, a full-speed control-failure default, hysteresis, isolation, and explicit dual-fan fault tests.
The design compares orientation alternatives and specifies direct-port placement, plug depth, bend radius, right-angle leads, P-clamps, strain transfer, and touch-remapping consequences.
Separate rear, bottom, display, filter, and microSD access paths preserve the installed cooler and avoid disturbing unrelated assemblies during routine service.

Eight configurable controller keys, replaceable legends, optional touch, accessible USB audio/MIDI connections, JACK-load testing, underrun logging, and microphone-oriented acoustic tests support repeated musical use.
The text does not claim a checkout, actual display identification, installed acoustic performance, or proven thermal capacity, and labels targets and manufacturer figures appropriately.

The plan includes dimensional auditing, STEP/scan checks, power-integrity review, thermal and fan-failure testing, airflow visualization, acoustics, signal integrity, RF, force tests, and safety checks.
The assumed display, separate prototype power, connector gutter, stack dimensions, airflow paths, materials, and modular service scheme remain mutually consistent.
arms.most_consequential_strength: The strongest balance of musician-facing controls, connector mechanics, cooling detail, maintenance, and verification planning.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The enclosure architecture is substantially shaped around an unverified RC070N display and initially requires two certified power inputs.

arms.label: Quartz
evidence: The Pi, cooler, NVMe, and fan are described precisely, but the compact HyperPixel GPIO stack is an unverified assumption and does not account for reported extra display-side USB-C connectors.
Commit-controlled repository facts, official hardware facts, inferences, explicit assumptions, and unresolved identities are clearly separated.
Two aligned intake paths cover the display, Active Cooler, Pi, SSD, and NVMe electronics before joining a sealed rear exhaust, with outlet area, filtering, and obstruction cases addressed.
The native cooler header is preserved and the independent rear-fan controller adds fusing, open-drain PWM, tach monitoring, and a full-speed reset or PWM-loss default.
Orientation alternatives, software and touch-axis implications, direct connector access, recess depth, plug envelope, bend radius, latch access, and cable anchoring are all specified.
The removable electronics cassette, separate fan hatch, sliding filter, microSD door, captive fasteners, and permanently retained Active Cooler support maintenance without unnecessary disassembly.

Five HID keys align with a documented profile while touch, mouse, and keyboard provide recovery; USB audio/MIDI power, JACK workloads, microphone noise, and repeated service cycles are included in validation.
The design explicitly identifies assumed components, acknowledges the failed clone, treats acoustic figures as free-air data, and makes no claim that fit or performance is proven.
Its risk table assigns concrete checks for fit, cooler clearance, FFC strain, plug variation, thermal load, fan failure, acoustics, power, input mapping, shutdown behavior, stability, and dust.

The concept is generally integrated, but fitting the extended-header display/cooler stack, NVMe assembly, fan duct, connector hood, hub, and controls into the 132 mm enclosure leaves unusually tight unverified packaging margins.
arms.most_consequential_strength: A compact design with excellent fail-safe fan control, recovery inputs, explicit connector envelopes, and a disciplined verification matrix.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The very tight enclosure and assumed extended-GPIO HyperPixel stack create the largest unresolved packaging and compatibility risk among the arms.

arms.label: Willow
evidence: The design accurately inventories native Pi hardware while treating the display, reported USB-C sockets, NVMe board, and SSD as unknowns accommodated through measured replaceable carriers.
Verified facts, reasonable inferences, explicit assumptions, unknown hardware, and provisional dimensions are consistently labeled and recorded.
The large filtered intake, quantified NVMe split, display and cooler wash, rear-left recombination, sealed fan chamber, clearance guidance, and failure scenarios provide a complete airflow model.
The Active Cooler retains firmware control and the independently fused rear fan has separate PWM/tach monitoring, temperature policy, recirculation control, and discharge-direction testing.

Orientation choices and cable routing are well reasoned, but the high-current USB-C panel pigtail and full-size HDMI adapter introduce extra connector motion and integrity risks absent from direct-access schemes.
Independent display and Pi/NVMe carriers, bottom and rear access, removable filter, service loops, and retention of the installed Active Cooler preserve unrelated hardware during repair.

Eight controller keys plus a separate native power key, replaceable legends, external audio/MIDI support, touch and mouse validation, acoustics, cable loading, and button-cycle tests address repeated musician use.
The design distinguishes sizing surrogates from identified parts, calls connector identities unresolved, labels fan data as free-air performance, and explicitly lists unproven outcomes.

The validation program covers hardware audit, power integrity, rotated UI behavior, multi-temperature thermal soak, fan and blockage faults, smoke testing, acoustics, mechanics, electrical safety, and wireless performance.
The modular carriers, generous envelope, component stack, right-side native ports, rear gallery, split cooling, weighted base, and manufacturing choices form a coherent whole.
arms.most_consequential_strength: Hardware-agnostic modularity preserves the unknown existing assembly while still delivering complete airflow, controls, service access, and validation.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: Panel-extending the 5 A USB-C power path and HDMI adds avoidable electrical and mechanical risk that must be validated or removed.

comparative_result: Harbor and Willow tie at 39/40. Harbor is strongest in musician interaction and direct connector mechanics; Willow is strongest in hardware-agnostic fidelity and modular preservation. Ember and Quartz tie at 38/40, with Ember offering the more spacious coherent package and Quartz the stronger compact recovery/control treatment but greater packaging risk.
disagreements: The closest judgment concerns hardware fidelity: all four responsibly disclose that the actual display and NVMe hardware are unknown, so scores distinguish how safely each design accommodates that uncertainty rather than treating any assumed component as verified. Willow's connector-extension penalty and Quartz's tight-package coherence penalty determine the narrow ranking.
